root_cause.text: A missing acquisition of `mr_table->route_list_lock` in `mlxsw_sp_mr_route_add()` during route replacement allowed an entry to be deleted from the multicast route list while `mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update()` concurrently traversed that list, causing a use-after-free of `mr_orig_route`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mutex_lock(&mr_table->route_list_lock)` and `mutex_unlock(&mr_table->route_list_lock)` specifically around `list_del(&mr_orig_route->node)`, and the commit message states “One instance of list entry deletion (during route replace) was missed,” while KASAN reports the freed object was released in `mlxsw_sp_mr_route_add` and later read in `mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect route list deletion with route_list_lock to avoid concurrent list corruption when removing an existing multicast route.
intent_record.what: The change adds a mutex_lock(&mr_table->route_list_lock) before list_del(&mr_orig_route->node) and a matching mutex_unlock(&mr_table->route_list_lock) after it in mlxsw_sp_mr_route_add().
intent_record.how: At runtime, removal of mr_orig_route from the route list is now performed under the route_list_lock, synchronizing this list modification with other concurrent accesses and preventing races or list corruption during route replacement/removal.

grouping_result.intent: Protect route list deletion with route_list_lock to avoid concurrent list corruption when removing an existing multicast route.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds route_list_lock protection around multicast route deletion during replacement, preventing concurrent traversal in mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update() from seeing a freed route entry.

candidates.rationale: This removes the route from the multicast route list without holding mr_table->route_list_lock, enabling concurrent traversal in mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update() to observe or follow a node being deleted, which is the direct list-manipulation step behind the use-after-free.
Immediately frees mr_orig_route after the unlocked list deletion, so a concurrent stats traversal that still references the list entry can dereference freed memory, producing the use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement removes mr_orig_route from the multicast route list without holding mr_table->route_list_lock during route replacement. That unlocked deletion races with concurrent traversal in mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update(), enabling the traversal to observe or follow a node being removed, which is the core condition leading to the use-after-free.

This statement frees mr_orig_route immediately after the unlocked list deletion. If mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update() is concurrently traversing the route list and still holds or reaches a reference to mr_orig_route, this free turns the race into a use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes both the route replacement path and the stats traversal over `mr_table->route_list`. In `mlxsw_sp_mr_route4_add()`, the replace path looks up `mr_orig_route`, adds the new route to `mr_table->route_list` via `list_add_tail(&mr_route->node, &mr_table->route_list);`, and then deletes the old route with `list_del(&mr_orig_route->node);` followed by `mlxsw_sp_mr_route4_destroy(mr_table, mr_orig_route);`. There is no acquisition of any `route_list_lock` (indeed this version of `struct mlxsw_sp_mr_table` has `struct list_head route_list;` but no lock member at all). Meanwhile, `mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update()` traverses the same list with `list_for_each_entry(mr_route, &mr_table->route_list, node)` and dereferences each route in `mlxsw_sp_mr_route_stats_update()`. Thus the vulnerable construct is present: route replacement removes and frees an entry from `route_list` without protecting the list against concurrent traversal. The fix is not present because there is no `mr_table->route_list_lock` in the table structure and no locking around list mutation in `mlxsw_sp_mr_route4_add()` or around traversal in `mlxsw_sp_mr_stats_update()`.
